subject: Iran
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Strait of Hormuz, using only its figures for 2011 (US Energy Information Administration), 2012 and 2023-2025. The arcs carry no values: the page names the biggest buyers (Japan, India, South Korea, China) but does not give each one's share. The strait lies between Iran and Oman; the map stays on the strait and does not show or name the islands Iran and the UAE dispute.

claims.text: The Strait of Hormuz provides the only sea passage from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.
During 2023–2025, 20% of the world's liquefied natural gas and 25% of seaborne oil trade passed through the strait annually.
According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, in 2011 an average of 14 tankers per day left the Persian Gulf through the strait carrying 17 million barrels of crude oil.
More than 85% of these crude oil exports went to Asian markets, with Japan, India, South Korea and China the largest destinations.
In July 2012 the UAE began using the Habshan–Fujairah oil pipeline, which bypasses the strait; it has a maximum capacity of around 2 million barrels per day.
All liquefied natural gas must be transported by ship through the strait.
